title: Plan Mode

body.text: read and plan, but not change anything yet
— it explores the code and proposes a detailed plan; you read it, adjust, then approve it to act. Great for big work or unfamiliar code.

example: "Press Shift+Tab to enter Plan Mode and ask 'what's needed to move from REST to GraphQL?' — you get a plan with nothing changed"

title: A good plan is half the work done

body.text: the cost of getting it wrong is high: legacy code, production systems, work across many modules
— read the plan and push back, like 'why this approach?' or 'is there a way without migrating the DB?'

example: "The plan proposes editing 12 files → ask 'can we narrow it to just one module first?' → get a lower-risk new plan"

options.text: Read and plan, but not edit files

question: When should you use Plan Mode?

options.text: Big work, unfamiliar code, or high cost of getting it wrong

question: You got a plan but disagree with parts. What can you do?

options.text: Push back and ask to adjust the plan before approving
You must always accept the plan

question: What's the benefit of Plan Mode?

options.text: Planning before acting makes big work clearer and lower-risk

question: What does 'a good plan is half the work done' mean?

options.text: A clear plan helps you act correctly and faster
